acceptance_checks.check: B1.3 — F-W0-004 conftest allowlist brittleness fix (third-recurrence mitigation)
acceptance_checks.evidence: Source-side guard added at src/aho/workstream_events.py: TestIsolationError class + _resolve_checkpoint_root() helper that, when PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST is set and AHO_TEST_CHECKPOINT_DIR is unset and find_project_root() returns a path outside the system tempdir, raises TestIsolationError loudly. Both emit_workstream_start and emit_workstream_complete refactored to call _resolve_checkpoint_root() and use narrow exception handlers (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) instead of bare `except Exception`. Conftest also sets AHO_TEST_CHECKPOINT_DIR=tmp_path for allowlisted modules. Tests at artifacts/tests/test_checkpoint_isolation_guard.py: 4 cases pass (guard raises with correct message; AHO_TEST_CHECKPOINT_DIR override accepted; tmpdir-resolved root accepted; real .aho-checkpoint.json mtime unchanged after guard fires). Belt-and-suspenders: allowlist provides positive isolation, source-side guard catches drift. The class is decorated with `__test__ = False` so pytest does not attempt to collect it as a test class.

podman 5.8.2 installed via pacman (post-Tailscale-DNS-fix; see F-host-001 for the detour). Rootless hello-world required a one-time fix for overlay-storage backing on ext4: installed fuse-overlayfs, ran `podman system reset --force` to clear the broken storage state, re-ran `podman run --rm hello-world` which returned the canonical Podman ASCII-art output. F-host-001 captures the DNS-detour record.

Package names resolved from pacman repos: nvidia-container-toolkit and libnvidia-container (no -base or vendor-qualifier suffix needed on CachyOS). Installation succeeded post-DNS-fix: `pacman -Qs nvidia-container` reports `local/libnvidia-container 1.19.0-1.1` and `local/nvidia-container-toolkit 1.19.0-1.1`. Note: /etc/cdi/ directory not yet created — sudo nvidia-ctk cdi generate is the next step but is blocked by the NVML driver/library version mismatch (B2.3 deferral).

Deferred across post-W0 reboot boundary per ADR 0007 §GPU passthrough deferral amendment. Empirical state: `sudo nvidia-ctk cdi generate --output=/etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml` fails with `failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch`. Root cause: pacman update brought userspace libraries to 595.71.05 (libnvidia-ml.so.595.71.05) while the running kernel still has the prior NVIDIA module loaded (595.58.03-class). Module reload mid-session reliably fails because Plasma/Wayland/X are using the modules. Reboot deferred to Sunday post-SF-queue per Kyle. Post-reboot validation is a one-command exercise: `sudo nvidia-ctk cdi generate --output=/etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml && podman run --rm --device nvidia.com/gpu=all docker.io/nvidia/cuda:12.0-base nvidia-smi` — expected: nvidia-smi from inside container reports the host GPU (RTX 2080 SUPER, 8 GB) and post-update driver 595.71.05. B2.3 is NOT on the W0/W3 critical path: ADR 0008 hybrid-mode dispatcher routes to host's native Ollama, which uses the host GPU directly with no container GPU passthrough required. Container GPU passthrough becomes load-bearing for production-tier (0.3.x) deployment.

acceptance_checks.check: B2.4 — host.containers.internal reachability probe (ADR 0008 hybrid-mode wire)
acceptance_checks.evidence: `podman run --rm alpine sh -c 'apk add curl >/dev/null 2>&1 && curl -sf -m 5 http://host.containers.internal:11434/api/version'` returned `{"version":"0.20.2"}`. Host Ollama was rebound from 127.0.0.1:11434 to 0.0.0.0:11434 via systemd drop-in /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/override.conf to satisfy the literal probe — see F-host-002 for the full record + accepted security trade-off + deferred firewall-rule mitigation (W3 alongside ADR 0008 implementation). DNS resolution of host.containers.internal works inside the container (resolves to 169.254.1.2, the netavark gateway). Wire was independently confirmed before the Ollama rebind via HTTP 301 from host.containers.internal:9090 (Jaeger UI) — proves the network path was not the blocker. The ADR 0008 hybrid-mode wire is verified end to end.

Full push+pull+delete cycle verified end to end against ghcr.io/soc-foundry/aho. Sequence: (1) `gh auth token | podman login ghcr.io -u SOCkjt --password-stdin` returned `Login Succeeded!` — token piped through stdin, never displayed in any tool output, never written to a repo file. (2) `podman tag aho:hello ghcr.io/soc-foundry/aho:hello-throwaway-w0-preflight` (exit 0). (3) `podman push ghcr.io/soc-foundry/aho:hello-throwaway-w0-preflight` succeeded — 5 blobs copied, manifest written to destination. (4) `podman rmi ghcr.io/soc-foundry/aho:hello-throwaway-w0-preflight` returned `Untagged`. (5) `podman pull ghcr.io/soc-foundry/aho:hello-throwaway-w0-preflight` re-fetched cleanly; pulled config sha matches the pushed image id (`f9954c7fd711d54069215e44db73118047e87cb0d2007b14f2be9893027b58da`); `podman run --rm <pulled-image> aho --version` returns `aho 0.2.14` — round-trip integrity preserved end to end. (6) Final local rmi clean. (7) Remote tag deletion via `gh api -X DELETE /orgs/soc-foundry/packages/container/aho/versions/836298903` rejected with HTTP 400: 'You cannot delete the last tagged version of a package. You must delete the package instead.' Per GitHub API guidance in the error body, executed `gh api -X DELETE /orgs/soc-foundry/packages/container/aho` (exit 0). Verified gone — `gh api /orgs/soc-foundry/packages/container/aho` returns HTTP 404 'Package not found.' Final state: local aho:hello intact (B3 deliverable), zero ghcr.io/soc-foundry/* local tags, remote package empty (W1's first push of `aho:0.2.17-rc1` will re-create it).

notes.soc_foundry_namespace: Verified via `gh api orgs/soc-foundry` to be type=Organization (display name 'SOC-Foundry'). API path for package operations is `/orgs/soc-foundry/packages/container/<name>`, not `/users/...`.
notes.github_api_constraint_recorded: GitHub does not allow deleting the last tagged version of a container package via `/versions/<id>` DELETE — instead requires deleting the entire package via `/packages/container/<name>` DELETE. This is GitHub API behavior, not a tooling issue. W1 should be aware: pushing `aho:0.2.17-rc1` re-creates the soc-foundry/aho package; tag deletions while >1 version exists work normally; deleting the last remaining tag requires the package-level delete (which W1's stable tags presumably won't need to invoke — only ephemeral preflight tags would).
notes.host_locality_history_preserved: First B2.5 attempt was blocked on gh-auth host-locality: Kyle's initial `gh auth login` landed on auraX9cos (the operator's starting shell), not NZXTcos (where the Podman build/push runs). gh credentials do not auto-sync between hosts. Re-running `gh auth login` on NZXTcos specifically resolved it. Recorded as historical context for future operators provisioning new hosts: gh auth + podman+ghcr work both need to land on the same host.
notes.gh_token_handling_pillar_11_compliance: Token consumed via `gh auth token | podman login --password-stdin` pipe only. Never displayed in any drafter-tool output. Never written to a file in the repo. Never read back into drafter context after the pipe completed. Username `SOCkjt` retrieved via `gh api user --jq .login` (does not return token).
